claims.text: Lumbar plexus: forms within psoas major, in front of the lumbar transverse processes.
claims.quote: course: formed within the substance of the psoas major muscle, anterior to the lumbar transverse processes

claims.text: Lumbar plexus branches: subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric (L1), ilioinguinal (L1), genitofemoral (L1, 2), lateral femoral cutaneous (L2, 3), femoral (L2, 3, 4), obturator (L2, 3, 4), and the lumbosacral trunk (L4, 5), which joins the sacral plexus.
claims.quote: subcostal nerve: T12 Iliohypogastric nerve: L1 ilioinguinal nerve: L1 genitofemoral nerve: L1, 2 lateral femoral cutaneous nerve: L2, 3 femoral nerve: L2, 3, 4 obturator nerve: L2, 3, 4 lumbosacral trunk: L4, 5 this contributes to the sacral plexus

claims.text: Lumbar plexus supply: motor to the lower limb and pelvic girdle; sensory to the lower anterior abdominal wall, groin, upper thigh and pudenda.
claims.quote: motor supply: lower limb and pelvic girdle sensory supply: lower anterior abdominal wall, groin, upper thigh and pudenda

claims.text: Sacral plexus: forms on the front of piriformis where the lumbosacral trunk (L4-5) joins the ventral rami of S1 to S4.
claims.quote: The sacral plexus forms on the anterior belly of the piriformis muscle and is formed by the lumbosacral trunk (L4-5) of the lumbar plexus, which enters the pelvis coursing medially to psoas major and unites with the ventral rami of the S1 to S4 nerve roots, which emerge from the anterior foramina of the sacrum.

claims.text: Sacral branches before the divisions: nerve to piriformis (S1-S2), perforating cutaneous nerve (S2-S3), posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (S1-S3), pelvic splanchnic (parasympathetic) nerves (S2-S4), pudendal nerve (S2-S4), perineal branch (S4).
claims.quote: nerve to piriformis (S1-S2) perforating cutaneous nerve (S2-S3) posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (S1-S3) parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) pudendal nerve (S2-S4) perineal branch (S4)

claims.text: Sacral anterior division: nerve to quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus (L4-S1), nerve to obturator internus and superior gemellus (L5-S2), and the tibial part of the sciatic nerve (L4-S3).
claims.quote: nerve to quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus muscles (L4-S1) nerve to internal obturator and superior gemellus muscles (L5-S2) tibial portion (L4-S3) of the sciatic nerve (L4-S3)
claims.locator: Branches: Anterior division of anterior rami

claims.text: Sacral posterior division: superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1), inferior gluteal nerve (L5-S2), and the common peroneal part of the sciatic nerve (L4-S2).
claims.quote: superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1) inferior gluteal nerve (L5-S2) common peroneal portion (L4-S2) of the sciatic nerve (L4-S3)
claims.locator: Branches: Posterior division of anterior rami

claims.text: Pudendal nerve: from S2-4; the nerve of the perineum and pelvic floor.
claims.quote: The pudendal nerve arises from the S2-4 nerve roots of the anterior division of the sacral plexus. It is the nerve of the perineum and pelvic floor.

claims.text: Pudendal nerve course: leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, turns around the sacrospinous ligament, passes through the lesser sciatic foramen and runs in the pudendal canal on the obturator fascia.
claims.quote: The nerve emerges from the pelvis and courses through the gluteal region through the greater sciatic foramen, below the piriformis muscle. It then turns forward around the sacrospinous ligament and leaves the gluteal region through the lesser sciatic foramen (between sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments). It is then directed into the pudendal canal, which lies on the obturator fascia above the falciform ridge on the ischial tuberosity.

claims.text: Pudendal nerve branches: inferior rectal nerve (perianal skin and external anal sphincter), dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris, and perineal nerve (superficial and deep perineal muscles and the external urethral sphincter).
claims.quote: The inferior rectal branch arches through the ischioanal fossa and reaches the perianal skin, as well as the external anal sphincter, supplying both. The dorsal nerve of penis/clitoris accompanies the dorsal artery to supply the clitoris or skin of the penis. It gives no branches in the deep pouch. The perineal branch gives off motor branches to superficial and deep perineal muscles and to the external urethral sphincter.
